title: Complementary immersions extend finite stratifications over a Noetherian scheme
statement:
Let $T$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], with $j(U)=|T|\setminus i(Z)$. Then $T,U,Z$ are Noetherian and quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; every subset of $|T|$ is quasi-compact, and $j$ is a quasi-compact morphism (the inverse image of each affine open is quasi-compact) [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].
For every finite stratification $(s_a:U_a\hookrightarrow U)_{a<n}$ [def-constructible-stratification], the family consisting of $(j\circ s_a:U_a\hookrightarrow T)_{a<n}$ and $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ is a finite stratification of $T$ by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-weil-constructible-subset]. For every finite stratification $(t_b:Z_b\hookrightarrow Z)_{b<m}$, the family consisting of $(i\circ t_b:Z_b\hookrightarrow T)_{b<m}$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ has the same property. In both cases the old stratum schemes and their maps into the source are unchanged; the listed maps into $T$ are the actual composites. The complementary scheme has its given scheme structure. Empty strata and an empty complementary scheme may be retained.

source.place: paragraph (3), parenthetical Noetherian quasi-compactness and the geometric preparation for immersion constructibility; original scalar-model immersion-extension proof steps 1–2

proof.text: Equip T with IsNoetherian using its given locally Noetherian and compact structures. Mathlib IsNoetherian.noetherianSpace gives a Noetherian underlying space, and NoetherianSpace.isCompact makes every subset compact, including every open, as in [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The open immersion j makes U locally Noetherian by isLocallyNoetherian_of_isOpenImmersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Its inducing map transports the Noetherian-space property to U, hence compactness, so U is Noetherian.

source.place: Tags 01OW (lemma-locally-Noetherian), 01OZ (lemma-Noetherian-topology); open-subscheme consequence stated by the cited existing Mathlib leaf

proof.text: Use NoetherianSpace.isCompact for every subset A of T, which is the open-cover argument of Stacks Tag 04ZA. The open immersion j is quasi-compact by the Mathlib instance for open immersions into a locally Noetherian target [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], equivalently by applying compactness to its inverse images of affine opens under the open embedding [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 04ZA (lemma-Noetherian-quasi-compact), proof of (1) implies (2); together with properties.tex Tag 01OX (lemma-immersion-into-noetherian), open case

proof.text: The closed immersion i is an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], hence locally of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft]. Apply LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to obtain locally Noetherian Z. The inducing map of its closed embedding transports the Noetherian-space property from T to Z, yielding CompactSpace Z and thus IsNoetherian Z. This uses the given Z and does not alter its structure sheaf.

source.place: Tag 02IK (lemma-locally-closed-in-Noetherian); locally finite type route: morphisms.tex Tags 01T5 and 01T6

proof.text: All three schemes $T,U,Z$ are locally Noetherian by the hypotheses and steps 1 and 3. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] separately to each of them: each intersection of two affine opens is quasi-compact, so each scheme is quasi-separated. Their quasi-compactness is already part of their established Noetherianity. Thus all three are qcqs.

The maps $s_a$ in a stratification of $U$, and $t_b$ in a stratification of $Z$, are immersions by [def-constructible-stratification]. Both $j$ and $i$ are immersions: for $j$ use the identity closed factor, and for $i$ the identity open factor, in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] gives immersions $j\circ s_a:U_a\to T$ and $i\circ t_b:Z_b\to T$. Use these actual composites as the new stratum maps, retaining $U_a,s_a$ and $Z_b,t_b$ themselves. Use $i:Z\to T$ or $j:U\to T$ itself for the additional stratum.

source.place: Tag 02V0 (lemma-composition-immersion), immersion-composition clause; construction follows blueprint det-lem-integral-models-operations paragraph (3)

proof.text: Every map constructed in step 5 is an immersion, so its range is locally closed by Scheme.Hom.isLocallyClosed_range [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-locally-closed-subset]. The same holds for the complementary immersion. Apply IsLocallyClosed.isConstructible_of_noetherianSpace from the proved source-library module WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Topology.Constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset]: an open is retrocompact since every subset of T is compact, and an open intersected with a closed set is constructible. Thus the ranges satisfy the local closedness and constructibility required by [def-constructible-stratification].

source.place: Tag 005L (lemma-constructible-Noetherian-space), proof from Tag 04ZA; locally closed image calculation is the subspace-topology argument of schemes.tex Tag 02V0

proof.text: For a stratification $(s_a)_{a<n}$ of $U$, index the extended family by $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\amalg\{*\}$. Give index $a$ the scheme $U_a$ and map $j\circ s_a$, and give $*$ the scheme $Z$ and map $i$. The images are $j(s_a(U_a))$ and $i(Z)$. Since $j$ is injective on points, distinct former images are disjoint. Each is contained in $j(U)$ and is therefore disjoint from $i(Z)$. Their union is $j(U)\cup i(Z)=|T|$, because the old images cover $U$ and the two given immersions are complementary. The $n+1$ images are locally closed and constructible by step 6 and their maps are immersions by step 5. These are exactly all requirements of [def-constructible-stratification].

source.place: Paragraph (3), constructibility preservation for open extension by zero; explicit geometric partition underlying that argument

proof.text: For a stratification $(t_b)_{b<m}$ of $Z$, use indices $\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\amalg\{*\}$, with scheme $Z_b$ and map $i\circ t_b$ at $b$, and scheme $U$ and map $j$ at $*$. Injectivity of $i$ makes the former images pairwise disjoint; they cover $i(Z)$ and avoid $j(U)$. The latter image is exactly their complement, so the $m+1$ images cover $T$ and are pairwise disjoint. Steps 5 and 6 give the required immersions and constructible locally closed images, proving the other assertion by [def-constructible-stratification]. In both constructions no new structure is imposed on an old stratum or on the complement: all source schemes and maps to $U$ or $Z$ are the original ones. Empty images satisfy the same disjointness and local-closedness checks. If $n=0$ then $U=\varnothing$ and the first family consists just of $i$; if $m=0$ then $Z=\varnothing$ and the second consists just of $j$. If the complementary scheme is empty its given immersion is simply retained as an empty stratum.

source.place: Paragraph (3), constructibility preservation for closed direct image; explicit geometric partition underlying that argument
